answer: An applicant locks collateral and is issued a one-use quill bound to that deposit. Admission is a scroll split into five clauses; each clause must be countersigned by a different tree in a published orchard of settled work-roots, and the quill is spent after those five strokes so it cannot be reused. Settlement then projects every applicant onto a ridge computed from host prefix, key family, and inter-clause timing. Any cluster sharing a ridge segment has its deposits burned and those orchard trees benched for two epochs, which makes cloned fleets expensive to land.
